text:
Beside the mother's bridal bed

a tender cradle sways,

the two loving spouses

invoke fortune

with celestial affection

for the sleeping child:

he dreams of the angels

he has just left.


The child's soft ecstasy

is seen in the tender face;

a loving, candid vow

is painted on the mother's;

on the father's somber face,

a pious thought…

May benevolent God

wish to hear their vows!


Her mystical vow

holds the sweetest wish:

to give, like a heavenly god,

an angel to the earth;

the father's thought

is violently stirred:

that a man, through his love,

has been given to the wretched world.


To the valley of tears,

be welcome, Alfredo,

where, without dreadful thorns,

as in a flower garden,

life may smile on you,

and the sun of joy

may always shine clear for you

without clouds of sorrow.


I do not want the poet's

sad, untamed genius

to inspire you,

the genius that clouds

his restless soul;

the power that inspires his lyre

with sacred fire

to drape his heart in bitterest grief.


I do not want glory's splendor,

though it be magnificent,

to drag you down a harsh path

after posthumous remembrance;

so dazzling a diadem

burns the ardent brow,

and it is a horrible, dropsical

thirst for ambition.


May the magical gleam

of riches not entice you;

for sordid greed

tarnishes and darkens

the soul's beauty,

and in it does not flower

the tree that gives life

to sweet charity.


May heaven free you from

that lethal wisdom

which gives genius

a sacrilegious altar of idolatry;

it does not see in man

a brother's heart,

and worships the idol

of vainglorious pride.


And if the peaceful path

of your precious life

by harsh brambles

should be obstructed;

may your pure soul become

like steel in hardship,

and may it firmly, fearlessly

challenge the struggle.


Do not shine like a Socrates

or a Redeemer Messiah

if the age of martyrs

is no longer granted to your days;

splendid and divine

was their destiny,

but sad it is on a Golgotha

to die… and not to save.


May your learning be worthy,

sweet child, and magnanimous;

may it shine, without twilight,

your ermine heart;

may thought not dry up

the flower of feeling,

and may sorrowful man inspire you

with love and compassion.


And when swift time,

after a pure existence,

carries you to the barren realm

of the dark region,

may family, homeland, and man

give laurels to your name,

and the archangels cry:

“Alfredo, blessing!”

translation.title: To the Child Alfredo H. and R.
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem’s extended benediction and its alternating maternal and paternal wishes; a slightly elliptical source phrase about the father’s “somber” face is kept as an image.
